OHD||St. Erasmus Cave Church.desc: Saint Erasmus Sveti Erazmo) is an ancient Christian basilica and necropolis located near Ohrid, North Macedonia, along the Ohrid-Struga freeway. Archaeological excavations have uncovered a three-part basilica and a necropolis with 124 graves dating from the 6th and 12th centuries.

SKP||Ristiḱ Palace.desc: Ristiḱ Palace is a monumental symbolic building at Macedonia Square in Skopje, North Macedonia.

LCA||Hala Sultan Tekke.desc: Hala Sultan Tekke is a mosque and takya on the west bank of Larnaca Salt Lake, in Larnaca, Cyprus. Umm Haram, known as Hala Sultan in Turkish tradition, was the wife of Ubada bin al-Samit, a companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, and foster sister of Muhammad's mother, Amina.

SKP||Stone Bridge.desc: The Stone Bridge is a bridge across the Vardar River in Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia, built by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror.

LCA||Ancient Kition.desc: Kition was an ancient Phoenician and Greek city-kingdom on the southern coast of Cyprus, one of the ten city-kingdoms of Cyprus.

LCA||Kamares Aqueduct.desc: Kamares Aqueduct, also known as the Bekir Pasha Aqueduct, is an aqueduct near Larnaca, Cyprus. Located just outside the city near the old road to Limassol, it was built between 1747 and 1750 and supplied Larnaca with fresh water for nearly two centuries.

LCA||Larnaca Synagogue.desc: The Larnaca Synagogue or Great Synagogue of Cyprus, also known as the Cyprus Central Synagogue, is a Hasidic Jewish congregation and synagogue, that is located at Apollodorou 4, in Larnaca, Cyprus. Designed in the Modernist style, the synagogue was completed in 2005.

LCA||Sourp Stepanos.desc: Sourp Stepanos Church is the Armenian Apostolic church in Larnaca, Cyprus.

PFO||Paphos Archaeological Park.desc: Paphos Archaeological Park is in Paphos, southwest Cyprus and contains the major part of its ancient Greek and Roman city. The park, still under excavation, is within the New Paphos section of the coastal city.

PFO||Paphos Archaeological Museum.desc: Paphos Archaeological Museum is a museum in Paphos, western Cyprus. It contains items ranging in age from the Neolithic to 1700 AD, with five rooms showcasing exhibits dating from the Neolithic era to the Middle Ages.

PFO||Basilica of Panagia Limeniotissa.desc: The Basilica of Panagia Limeniotissa is a ruined basilica in Paphos, Cyprus. It was built at the beginning of the 5th century and it is dedicated to "Our Lady of the Harbour".

MLA||Great Siege Monument.desc: The Great Siege Monument, also known as the Monument to the Fallen of the Great Siege, is a monument commemorating the Great Siege of Malta located in Valletta, Malta. It consists of three bronze figures symbolizing Faith, Fortitude, and Civilization, standing on top of a granite base.

MLA||Auberge d'Aragon.desc: The Auberge d'Aragon is an auberge in Valletta, Malta. It was built in 1571 to house knights of the Order of Saint John from the langue of Aragon, Navarre and Catalonia.

MLA||National Library of Malta.desc: The National Library of Malta, often known as the Bibliotheca, is a reference library in Republic Square, Valletta, Malta. It was founded by Grand Master Emmanuel de Rohan-Polduc in 1776 out of the collections of the knight Louis Guérin de Tencin.

MLA||Casa Rocca Piccola.desc: Casa Rocca Piccola is a 16th-century palace in Malta, and home of the noble Maltese family de Piro. It is situated in Valletta, the capital city of Malta.

MLA||Nibbia Chapel.desc: The Nibbia Chapel was a Roman Catholic chapel in Valletta, Malta, which was dedicated to Our Lady of Mercy. It was originally built in 1619 by Fra Giorgio Nibbia, a knight of the Order of St.

PFO||Sanctuary of Aphrodite.desc: The Sanctuary of Aphrodite Paphia was a sanctuary in ancient Paphos on Cyprus dedicated to the goddess Aphrodite. Located where the legendary birth of Aphrodite took place, it has been referred to as the main sanctuary of Aphrodite, and was a place of pilgrimages in the ancient world for centuries.

PRN||Incident at Pristina airport.desc: The incident at the Pristina airport was a military confrontation between the forces of Russia and NATO from 11 to 13 June 1999, immediately following the end of the Kosovo War. Russian troops unexpectedly occupied the airport ahead of a planned NATO deployment, creating a tense stand-off.

MLA||Palace Armoury.desc: The Palace Armoury is an arms collection housed at the Grandmaster's Palace in Valletta, Malta. It was the main armoury of the Order of St.

MLA||Fort St. Elmo.desc: Fort Saint Elmo is a star fort in Valletta, Malta. It stands on the seaward shore of the Sciberras Peninsula that divides Marsamxett Harbour from Grand Harbour, and commands the entrances to both harbours along with Fort Tigné and Fort Ricasoli.

FAE||Sandavágur Church.desc: Sandavágur Church is a distinctive red-roofed church in the town of Sandavágur in the Faroe Islands.

KIV||Botanical Garden.desc: The Chișinău Botanical Garden of the Academy of Sciences of Moldova is a botanical research institution and public garden located in the Botanica sector of Chișinău, Moldova.

KIV||Chișinău Zoo.desc: The Chișinău Botanical Garden of the Academy of Sciences of Moldova is a botanical research institution and public garden located in the Botanica sector of Chișinău, Moldova.

PRN||Kosovo Railways Museum.desc: Kosovo Polje or Fushë Kosova is a city and municipality located in the District of Pristina in Kosovo. The municipality has an area of 84.09 km2 (32.47 sq mi) and in 2024 had 63,949 inhabitants making it the eighth most populous municipality in Kosovo.

FAE||Vørðufelli.desc: Vørðufelli is a mountain overlooking the village of Sørvágur on the Faroe Islands. Its height is 284 metres above sea level.

KIV||Biserica de lemn.desc: Wooden church of the Dormition of Mary of Hirișeni is a religious building built in 1642. As of today, the church is preserved in the Village museum of Chișinău, Republic of Moldova.

FAE||Eysturtindur.desc: Eysturtindur is the second highest point - 714 m - on the island of Vágoy, Faroe Islands.

JER||Jersey Zoo.desc: Jersey Zoo is a zoological park established in 1959 on the island of Jersey in the English Channel by naturalist and writer Gerald Durrell. It is operated by the Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust.

JER||Grouville Hoard.desc: The Grouville Hoard is a hoard of an estimated 70,000 late Iron Age (Celtic) and Roman coins reported in June 2012. They were discovered by metal detectorists Reg Mead and Richard Miles in a field at an undisclosed location in the parish of Grouville on the east side of Jersey in the Channel Islands.

JER||Hohlgangsanlage 8.desc: Hohlgangsanlage 8 was a partially completed underground hospital complex in St. Lawrence, Jersey, built by German occupying forces during the occupation of Jersey during World War II.

JER||Les Platons.desc: Les Platons is the highest point of Jersey, a British Crown dependency, with an elevation of 136 metres (446 ft). It is located in the Vingtaine de la Ville-à-l'Évêque in the parish of Trinity.

JER||Samares Manor.desc: Samarès Manor is a manor house with medieval origins in the Vingtaine de Samarès, in the parish of St. Clement in Jersey, and is the traditional home of the Seigneur de Samarès.

JER||La Tour de Vinde.desc: La Tour de Vinde is a Martello tower that the British erected between 1808 and 1810 to command the approaches to St Aubin's Bay, Jersey. The tower stands at the foot of the cliffs of Noirmont Point, in the Vingtaine de Noirmont in the Parish of Saint Brélade.

FAE||Sandavágur stone.desc: Vágar is one of the 18 islands in the archipelago of the Faroe Islands and the most westerly of the large islands. With a size of 178 square kilometres, it ranks third in size, behind Streymoy and Eysturoy.

FAE||Lítli Drangur.desc: Vágar is one of the 18 islands in the archipelago of the Faroe Islands and the most westerly of the large islands. With a size of 178 square kilometres, it ranks third in size, behind Streymoy and Eysturoy.

GCI||Castle Cornet.desc: Castle Cornet is a large island castle in Guernsey, and former tidal island, also known as Cornet Rock or Castle Rock. Its importance was as a defence not only of the island, but of the roadstead.

GCI||Hauteville House.desc: Hauteville House is a house in St. Peter Port, Guernsey.

GCI||Little Chapel.desc: The Little Chapel is situated in the Les Vauxbelets valley, Saint Andrew, Guernsey. It was created in July 1914, by Brother Déodat.

GCI||Bréhon Tower.desc: The Bréhon Tower is accessible only by boat and sits on Bréhon Rock, an island in the Little Russell channel about 1.5 km northeast of St Peter Port, Guernsey, between the port and the islands of Herm and Jethou. Thomas Charles de Putron (1806–1869) built the oval tower of granite from Herm, completing the work in 1857.

PRN||Kalaja e Harilaqit.desc: Harilaq is a village in the municipality of Fushë Kosovë, Kosovo.

GCI||Fort Saumarez.desc: Fort Saumarez is a Martello tower in Saint Peter, Guernsey, on a headland that forms the northern tip of L'Erée and extends to the Lihou causeway.

GCI||Fort Grey.desc: Fort Grey, colloquially known as the "cup and saucer", is a Martello tower located on a tidal rock in Rocquaine Bay in Saint Peter, Guernsey on the west coast of the island.

ACI||Ortac.desc: Ortac is a small uninhabited islet about 5 kilometres west of the coast of Alderney near to the islet of Burhou. It measures roughly 50 by 70 metres, and rises 24 metres above the sea level.

GCI||Vale Castle.desc: Vale Castle, is a protected building located in the Vale, Guernsey. The original name was "Le Château St Michel", later it became "Château de Val" or "Château de Valle" and is over 1,000 years old.

FAE||Bøsdalafossur.desc: Bøsdalafossur is a waterfall in the Faroe Islands that flows from the lake Sørvágsvatn/Leitissvatn into the Atlantic Ocean. It has a height of 30 meters.

ACI||Alderney Railway.desc: The Alderney Railway on Alderney is the only railway in the Bailiwick of Guernsey, and the only working railway in the Channel Islands. The Alderney Railway opened in 1847 and runs for about 2 miles (3.2 km), mostly following a coastal route, from Braye Road to Mannez Quarry and Lighthouse.

ACI||Fort Tourgis.desc: Fort Tourgis is an extensive fortification in Alderney to the north west of St Anne forming part of the Fortifications of Alderney inside the Bailiwick of Guernsey.

IOM||Diocese of Sodor and Man.desc: The Diocese of Sodor and Man is a diocese of the Church of England. It is one of only two Church of England dioceses not within the United Kingdom.

IOM||Laxey Wheel.desc: The Laxey Wheel is built into the hillside above the village of Laxey in the Isle of Man. It is the largest surviving original working waterwheel in the world.

IOM||Snaefell.desc: Snaefell is the highest mountain and the only summit above 2,000 feet (610 m) on the Isle of Man, at 2,037 feet (620.9 m) above sea level. The summit is crowned by a railway station, cafe, several communications masts and can be reached by narrow gauge railway.

BRN||Lohn Castle.desc: The Lohn Estate is a manor and estate located in Kehrsatz, canton of Bern, Switzerland. It serves as the official estate of the Swiss Federal Council.

IOM||St Trinian's Church.desc: St Trinian's Church is the roofless ruin of a small chapel at the foot of Greeba Mountain, adjacent to the main A1 Douglas - Peel Road in the parish of Marown, Isle of Man.

JER||Grouville Church.desc: Grouville Church is one of the twelve ancient parish churches in the island of Jersey; it is sited in the eastern parish of Grouville. It is a Grade I Jersey listed building.

BRN||Auguetbrücke.desc: The Auguetbrücke is a 60-metre-long covered wooden bridge over the Aare River between Muri bei Bern and Belp in the Swiss canton of Bern. Originally constructed in 1836 and later relocated to its present site, it now serves as a pedestrian crossing and occasional event venue.

BRN||Kehrsatz Castle.desc: Kehrsatz Castle is a castle in the municipality of Kehrsatz of the canton of Bern in Switzerland.

BRN||Villa Mettlen.desc: The Villa Mettlen is a country estate in the municipality of Muri bei Bern in the Canton of Bern in Switzerland. The grounds comprise 15,466 m2, of which the building footprint is 499 m2.

BRN||Schloss Wittigkofen.desc: Wittigkofen Castle is a castle in the municipality of Bern of the Canton of Bern in Switzerland. It is a Swiss heritage site of national significance.

BOO||Bodø Station.desc: Bodø Station is a railway station located in the center of the town of Bodø in Bodø Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. The station is the terminus of the Nordland Line that was completed in 1961.

BOO||Nordlandsmuseet.desc: Nordland Museum is a museum located in the center of Bodø in Nordland, Norway. The museum is a central part of a larger consortium of 18 museum units in nine municipalities with the county of Nordland.

AES||Giske kyrkje.desc: Giske Church is a 12th-century marble parish church of the Church of Norway in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located on the south side of the island of Giske, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) northwest of the town of Ålesund.

BOO||Bodin kirke.desc: Bodin Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Bodø Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the southeastern part of the town of Bodø.

BOO||Bodø Cathedral.desc: Bodø Cathedral is a cathedral of the Church of Norway in Bodø Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the town of Bodø.

INV||Cawdor Castle.desc: Cawdor Castle is a castle in the parish of Cawdor in Nairnshire, Scotland. It is built around a 15th-century tower house, with substantial additions in later centuries.

INV||Kilravock Castle.desc: Kilravock Castle is located near the village of Croy, between Inverness and Nairn, in the council area of Highland, Scotland. It was begun around 1460 and has been the seat of the Clan Rose since that time.

AES||Vigra kyrkje.desc: Vigra Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located on the island of Vigra, about 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) southwest of the village of Roald.

INV||Chanonry Lighthouse.desc: Chanonry Point lies at the end of Chanonry Ness, a spit of land extending into the Moray Firth between Fortrose and Rosemarkie on the Black Isle, Scotland.

AES||Valderøy Church.desc: Valderøy Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located on the south side of the village of Nordstrand on the island of Valderøya.

INV||Culloden Battlefield.desc: The Battle of Culloden took place on 16 April 1746, near Inverness, in the Scottish Highlands. A Jacobite army under Charles Edward Stuart was decisively defeated by a British government force commanded by the Duke of Cumberland, thereby ending the Jacobite rising of 1745.

INV||Fortrose Cathedral.desc: Fortrose Cathedral was the episcopal seat (cathedra) of the medieval Scottish diocese of Ross in the Highland region of Scotland near the city of Inverness.

INV||Castle Stuart.desc: Castle Stuart is a restored tower house on the banks of the Moray Firth, about 6.5 miles (10 km) northeast of Inverness.

INV||Dalcross Castle.desc: Dalcross Castle is a restored 17th century tower house, about 1+1⁄2 miles southwest of Croy, Highland, Scotland, and about 7 miles northeast of Inverness. The castle stands on a ridge.

gem:bruges||Provinciaal Hof.desc: The Provinciaal Hof is a neo-Gothic building on the Markt in Bruges, Belgium. It is the former meeting place for the Provincial Government of West Flanders.

gem:bruges||Basilica of the Holy Blood.desc: The Basilica of the Holy Blood is a Roman Catholic basilica in Bruges, Belgium. The church houses a relic of the Holy Blood that was, according to tradition, collected by Joseph of Arimathea and brought from the Holy Land by Thierry of Alsace, Count of Flanders.

gem:bruges||St. Donatian's Cathedral.desc: St. Donatian's Cathedral was a Roman Catholic cathedral in Bruges, Belgium.

gem:bruges||Frietmuseum.desc: The Frietmuseum is a museum in Bruges, Belgium, which is devoted to the history of potatoes and the production of Belgian fries. It describes itself as "the first and only museum dedicated to potato fries".

gem:bruges||Basilique du Saint-Sang.desc: The Basilica of the Holy Blood is a Roman Catholic basilica in Bruges, Belgium. The church houses a relic of the Holy Blood that was, according to tradition, collected by Joseph of Arimathea and brought from the Holy Land by Thierry of Alsace, Count of Flanders.

gem:ghent||Saint Bavo Cathedral.desc: Saint Bavo's Cathedral, also known as Sint-Baafs Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Ghent, Belgium. The 89-metre-tall (292 ft) Gothic building is the seat of the Diocese of Ghent and is named for Saint Bavo of Ghent.

gem:ghent||Dulle Griet.desc: The Dulle Griet is a medieval large-calibre gun founded in Ghent.

gem:ghent||Graslei.desc: Graslei is a quay in the historic city center of Ghent, Belgium, located on the right bank of the Leie river. The quay opposite of the Graslei is called Korenlei.

gem:bruges||Provostry of St. Donatian.desc: The Provostry of St. Donatian is a Baroque building on the Burg Square in Bruges, Belgium.

gem:ghent||Ghent City Hall.desc: The City Hall of Ghent, East Flanders, Belgium, is a four-sided complex surrounded by the Botermarkt, the Hoogpoort, the Stadhuissteeg and the Poeljemarkt. The main wings are the late-Gothic alderman's house of De Keure and the alderman's house of Gedele in the Renaissance style.

gem:ghent||Geeraard de Duivelsteen.desc: The Geeraard de Duivelsteen is a 13th-century gothic architecture building in Ghent, Belgium. It served as defense of the Portus Ganda, the city's port.

gem:antwerp||Het Steen.desc: Het Steen is a medieval fortress in the old city centre of Antwerp, Belgium, one of Europe's biggest ports. The surviving structure was built between 1200 and 1225 as a gateway to a larger castle of the Dukes of Brabant which was demolished in the 19th century.

gem:antwerp||Boerentoren.desc: The Boerentoren is a historic high-rise building in Antwerp, Belgium. Constructed between 1929 and 1932 and originally 87.5 m (287 ft) high, it remained the tallest building and the second-tallest structure in the city until 2019, when the Antwerp Tower surpassed it with a height of 100.7 m (330 ft).

gem:antwerp||Rubenshuis.desc: The Rubenshuis is the former home and workshop of Peter Paul Rubens (1577–1640) in Antwerp. Purchased in 1610, Rubens had the Flemish townhouse renovated and extended on the basis of designs by Rubens himself.

gem:antwerp||Plantin-Moretus House-Works.desc: The Plantin–Moretus Museum is a printing museum in Antwerp, Belgium which focuses on the work of the 16th-century printers Christophe Plantin and Jan Moretus. It is located in their former residence and printing establishment, the Plantin Press, at the Vrijdagmarkt in Antwerp, and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2005.

gem:antwerp||Stadhuis Antwerpen.desc: The City Hall of Antwerp, Belgium, stands on the western side of that city's Grote Markt. Erected between 1561 and 1565, after designs made by Cornelis Floris de Vriendt and several other architects and artists, this Renaissance building incorporates both Flemish and Italian influences.

gem:antwerp||Bourla.desc: Bourla Theatre is a theatre located in Antwerp that seats around 900. The building is designed in a neoclassical style on the site of the former Tapissierspand tapestry market.

gem:utrecht||Traiectum.desc: Traiectum was a Roman fort, on the frontier of the Roman Empire in Germania Inferior. The remains of the fort are in the center of Utrecht, Netherlands, which takes its name from the fort.

gem:rotterdam||Beurs-World Trade Center.desc: Beurs-World Trade Center is located on the Coolsingel and Beursplein in the centre of Rotterdam.

gem:utrecht||Domkerk.desc: The historic Diocese of Utrecht was a diocese of the Latin Church of the Catholic Church from 695 to 1580, and from 1559 archdiocese in the Low Countries before and during the Protestant Reformation.

gem:rotterdam||Lijnbaan.desc: The Lijnbaan is the main shopping street of Rotterdam. It was opened in 1953, as the main pedestrian street in the new shopping district, after the old shopping district was completely destroyed during the bombing of Rotterdam by the German Luftwaffe.

gem:utrecht||Vismarkt 4, Utrecht.desc: Galeries Modernes was a department store chain in the Netherlands in the 20th century, with roots in the earlier company Grand Bazar Français. The last branches were closed in 1984.

gem:rotterdam||Museum Rotterdam.desc: The Museum Rotterdam, until 2011 called the Historical Museum Rotterdam, is a museum about the history of Rotterdam located at the Coolhaven.

gem:utrecht||Academiegebouw.desc: Utrecht University is a public research university in Utrecht, Netherlands. Established 26 March 1636, it is one of the oldest universities in the Netherlands.

gem:rotterdam||De Bijenkorf.desc: De Bijenkorf is a chain of high-end department stores in the Netherlands, with its flagship store on Dam Square in Amsterdam. The chain is owned by Selfridges Group, owner also of Britain's Selfridges and Ireland's Brown Thomas and Arnotts.

gem:haarlem||Haarlem.desc: Haarlem is a city and municipality in the Netherlands. It is the capital of the province of North Holland.

gem:haarlem||Hofje van Noblet.desc: The Hofje van Noblet is a hofje in Haarlem, Netherlands.

gem:haarlem||Hofje van Staats.desc: The Hofje van Staats is a hofje in Haarlem, Netherlands, on the Jansweg 39, close to the Haarlem railway station.

gem:delft||City Centre.desc: Delft is a city and municipality in the province of South Holland, Netherlands. It is located between Rotterdam, to the southeast, and The Hague, to the northwest.

gem:zaanse-schans||Het Jonge Schaap.desc: Het Jonge Schaap is the name of a wooden wind powered sawmill, located in the Zaanse Schans, in the municipality of Zaanstad.

gem:delft||Markt.desc: Delft is a city and municipality in the province of South Holland, Netherlands. It is located between Rotterdam, to the southeast, and The Hague, to the northwest.

gem:haarlem||Koepelgevangenis.desc: The Koepelgevangenis is a former prison in Haarlem, Netherlands. It is one of three Panopticon-style buildings situated in the country.

gem:zaanse-schans||De Gekroonde Poelenbu.desc: De Gekroonde Poelenburg is a paltrok mill in Zaandam, Netherlands which has been restored to working order. Like all Dutch paltrok mills it is a wind-powered sawmill.

gem:zaanse-schans||De Os.desc: De Os is an oil windmill in the Zaanse Schans, Zaanstad.

gem:zaanse-schans||De Zoeker.desc: De Zoeker is the name of an oil windmill, located in the Zaanse Schans, Zaanstad. Its purpose is to press seeds such as linseed and rapeseed into vegetable oil.

gem:delft||Hugo Grotius.desc: Hugo Grotius, also known as Hugo de Groot or Huig de Groot, was a Dutch humanist, diplomat, lawyer, theologian, jurist, statesman, poet and playwright. A teenage prodigy, he was born in Delft and studied at Leiden University.

gem:zaanse-schans||Het Klaverblad.desc: Het Klaverblad is a small wooden saw mill, located in the Zaanse Schans, in the municipality of Zaanstad.

gem:heidelberg||Kornmarkt-Madonna.desc: The Kornmarkt-Madonna is a fountain sculpture in the Kornmarkt in the Altstadt of Heidelberg. It is also known as the Mariensäule and Muttergottesbrunnen.

gem:heidelberg||President Friedrich Eber.desc: The President Friedrich Ebert Foundation Memorial in Heidelberg is a non-partisan foundation financed by the German Federal Government. It commemorates the life and work of Friedrich Ebert, who was born in the house on 4 February 1871.

gem:rothenburg||St. Jakob.desc: Rothenburg ob der Tauber is a town located in the district of Ansbach of Mittelfranken, the Franconia region of Bavaria, Germany. It is well known for its well-preserved medieval old town, a destination for tourists from around the world.

gem:heidelberg||Alte Universität (Heidel.desc: The Old University is an important baroque building of the University of Heidelberg located between the Hauptstrasse and the Universitätsplatz in the old town of Heidelberg.

gem:regensburg||Regensburg Hauptbahnhof.desc: Regensburg Hauptbahnhof is the main railway station in the city of Regensburg in southern Germany.

gem:bamberg||Altes Rathaus.desc: Bamberg is a town in Upper Franconia, Bavaria, Germany, on the river Regnitz close to its confluence with the river Main. Bamberg had 79,000 inhabitants in 2022.

gem:garmisch||Mittenwaldbahn.desc: The Mittenwald Railway, popularly known as the Karwendelbahn, is a railway line in the Alps in Austria and Germany. It connects Innsbruck via Seefeld and Mittenwald to Garmisch-Partenkirchen.

gem:neuschwanstein||Neuschwanstein Castl.desc: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill of the foothills of the Alps in the very south of Germany, near the border with Austria.

gem:regensburg||Meier Max Wolff.desc: The Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize, or Leibniz Prize, is awarded by the German Research Foundation to "exceptional scientists and academics for their outstanding achievements in the field of research".

gem:regensburg||Peterskirchlein.desc: Johannes Kepler was a German polymath who was an astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and music theorist. He is a key figure in the 17th-century Scientific Revolution, best known for his laws of planetary motion, and his books Astronomia nova, Harmonice Mundi, and Epitome Astronomiae Copernicanae.

gem:neuschwanstein||Schloss Neuschwanste.desc: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill of the foothills of the Alps in the very south of Germany, near the border with Austria.

gem:neuschwanstein||Marienbrücke.desc: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill of the foothills of the Alps in the very south of Germany, near the border with Austria.

gem:baden-baden||Baden-Baden.desc: Baden-Baden is a spa town in the state of Baden-Württemberg, south-western Germany, at the north-western border of the Black Forest mountain range on the small river Oos, ten kilometres east of the Rhine, the France–Germany border, and forty kilometres north-east of Strasbourg, France.

gem:neuschwanstein||Hohenschwangau Castl.desc: Hohenschwangau Castle is a 19th-century palace in southern Germany. It was built by King Maximilian II of Bavaria, and was the childhood residence of his son, King Ludwig II of Bavaria.

gem:garmisch||St. Martin.desc: The 1936 Winter Olympics, officially known as the IV Olympic Winter Games and commonly known as Garmisch-Partenkirchen 1936, were a winter multi-sport event held from 6 to 16 February 1936 in the market town of Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Germany. Later that year, the country also hosted the 1936 Summer Olympics, which were held in Berlin.

gem:baden-baden||Trinkhalle.desc: The Trinkhalle in the Kurhaus spa complex in Baden-Baden, Germany was built 1839–42 by Heinrich Hübsch in a complementary architectural style as the spa's main building. The 90-metre arcade is lined with frescos and benches.

gem:baden-baden||Lichtentaler Allee.desc: The Lichtentaler Allee is a historic park and arboretum, set out as a 2.3 kilometer strolling avenue along the west bank of the river Oos in Baden-Baden, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It is open daily without charge.

gem:baden-baden||Theater Baden-Baden.desc: Theater Baden-Baden at Goetheplatz is the city theater of Baden-Baden in the Black Forest in Baden-Württemberg, Germany built between 1860 and 1862.

gem:dresden-saxon||Königstein Fortress.desc: Königstein Fortress, the "Saxon Bastille", is a hilltop fortress near Dresden, in Saxon Switzerland, Germany, above the town of Königstein on the left bank of the River Elbe. It is one of the largest hilltop fortifications in Europe and sits atop the table hill of the same name.

gem:dresden-saxon||Lilienstein.desc: Lilienstein is a highly distinctive mountain in Saxon Switzerland, in Saxony, southeastern Germany, and was once the site of a Bohemian castle. It is one of the few table mountains on the east of the river Elbe and constitutes the symbol of the Saxon Switzerland National Park.

gem:dresden-saxon||Pfaffenstein.desc: The Pfaffenstein, formerly called the Jungfernstein, is a table hill, 434.6 m (1,426 ft) above sea level, in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains in Saxony. It lies west of the River Elbe near Königstein and is also referred to as "Saxon Switzerland in miniature" on account of its diverse structure.

gem:dresden-saxon||Barbarine.desc: The Barbarine is the best-known free-standing rock formation in the German part of the Elbe Sandstone Mountains. It is a rock pinnacle, 42.7 metres (140 ft) high, and is the symbol of Saxon Switzerland.

gem:karlovy-vary||Karlovy Vary.desc: Karlovy Vary is a spa city in the Karlovy Vary Region of the Czech Republic. It has about 49,000 inhabitants.

gem:geiranger||Geirangerfjord.desc: Geirangerfjorden (Norwegian) or Geiranger Fjord (English) is a fjord in the Sunnmøre region of Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located entirely in Stranda Municipality.

gem:eger||Archbishop's Garden.desc: Archbishop's Garden is a park in Eger, Hungary, that covers about 12 hectares.

gem:eger||Archbishop's Palace.desc: Eger is the county seat of Heves County, and the second largest city in Northern Hungary. A city with county rights, Eger is best known for its medieval castle, thermal baths, baroque buildings, the northernmost Ottoman minaret, and red wines.

gem:geiranger||Skageflå.desc: Skageflå is one of a handful of historic mountain farms on the steep mountainsides along the Geirangerfjorden. It is located in Stranda Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway.

gem:geiranger||Geiranger kyrkje.desc: Geiranger Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Stranda Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located in the village of Geiranger, and the end of the famous Geirangerfjorden.

gem:eger||Cathedral Basilica of St. John.desc: The Cathedral Basilica of St. John the Apostle or more formally Metropolitan Cathedral Basilica of St.

gem:geiranger||Dalsnibba.desc: Dalsnibba is a mountain in Stranda Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located at the end of the Geiranger valley, about 7 km (4 mi) south of the village of Geiranger and the Geirangerfjorden.

gem:bergen-nearby||Vik kyrkje.desc: Vik Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Vik Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Vikøyri.

gem:lofoten||Stamsund kirke.desc: Stamsund Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Vestvågøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Stamsund on the island of Vestvågøya.

gem:lofoten||Buksnes kirke.desc: Buksnes Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Vestvågøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Gravdal on the island of Vestvågøya.

gem:bergen-nearby||Hove kyrkje.desc: Hove Church is a historic parish church of the Church of Norway in Vik Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Vikøyri on the Arnafjord, an arm of the Sognefjord.

gem:kiruna||Kiirunavaara.desc: Kiirunavaara is a mountain situated in Kiruna Municipality in Norrbotten County, Sweden. It contains one of the largest and richest bodies of iron ore in the world.

gem:bergen-nearby||Hopperstad stavkyrkje.desc: Hopperstad Stave Church is a historic parish church of the Church of Norway in the village of Vikøyri in Vik Municipality in Vestland county. It was historically the church for the Hopperstad parish in the Diocese of Bjørgvin.

gem:visby||Solberga Abbey.desc: Solberga Abbey, was a Cistercian nunnery in Sweden, in operation from 1246 until at least 1469. It was located outside Visby on Gotland until 1404, and then in Visby.

gem:kiruna||Kiruna kyrka.desc: Kiruna Church is a church building in Kiruna, Sweden, and is one of Sweden's largest wooden buildings. The church was built between 1909 and 1912, designed by the architect Gustaf Wickman.

gem:dalarna||Falun Mine.desc: Falun Mine was a mine in Falun, Sweden, that operated for a millennium from the 10th century to 1992. It produced as much as two-thirds of Europe's copper needs and helped fund many of Sweden's wars in the 17th century.

gem:kiruna||Kirunas gamla centralstation.desc: Kiruna Station is a railway station located on the Iron Ore Line in Kiruna, Sweden. The station is served by up to three daily services northwards on the Iron Ore Line to Narvik Station in Norway.

gem:visby||Slaget vid Visby.desc: The Battle of Visby was fought in 1361 near the town of Visby on the island of Gotland, Sweden, between the forces of the Danish king and the Gutnish country yeomen. The Danish force was victorious.

gem:vik||Reynisdrangar.desc: Reynisdrangar are the basalt sea stacks situated under the mountain Reynisfjall near the village of Vík í Mýrdal in southern Iceland. It is framed by a black sand beach that was ranked in 1991 as one of the ten most beautiful non-tropical beaches in the world.

gem:vik||Dyrhólaey lighthouse.desc: The Dyrhólaey Lighthouse is a lighthouse located on the central south coast of Iceland.

gem:skaftafell||Svartifoss.desc: Svartifoss is a waterfall in Skaftafell in Vatnajökull National Park in Iceland, and is one of the most popular sights in the park. It is surrounded by dark lava columns, which gave rise to its name.

gem:skaftafell||Skaftafell.desc: Skaftafell is a preservation area in Öræfi, southeast Iceland. It was once a major farm, later being named a national park.

gem:skaftafell||Kristínartindar.desc: Kristínartindar is a mountain in Vatnajökull National Park, Iceland. It has a height of 1,126 m above sea level and its knife-edge summit straddles two glacier valleys.

gem:brasov||Battle of Braşov.desc: The Battle of Brașov was fought on July 17, 1603, between the troops of Wallachia led by Radu Șerban and the Habsburg monarchy on one side and the Transylvanian troops led by Mózes Székely on the other side.

gem:brasov||Castra of Brașov.desc: The Castra of Brașov was a fort in the Roman province of Dacia near Brașov, Romania, on Șprenghi Hill.

gem:sighisoara||Historic Centre of Sighi.desc: The Historic Centre of Sighișoara is the old historic center of the town of Sighișoara, Romania, built in the 12th century by Saxon settlers. It is an inhabited medieval citadel that, in 1999, was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its 850-year-old testament to the history and culture of the Transylvanian Saxons.

gem:sighisoara||School on the Hill.desc: The School on the Hill is an educational institution in Sighișoara, Romania. It is located next to the covered wooden Stairs, bears Schola Seminarium Republicae and is dated 1619.

gem:sighisoara||Entry of the Theotokos i.desc: The Entry of the Theotokos into the Temple Church is a Romanian Orthodox church located at 22 Ecaterina Varga Street, Sighișoara, Romania. It is dedicated to the Entry of the Theotokos into the Temple.

gem:brasov||Saxon Lutheran church in Bra.desc: Brașov County is a county (județ) of Transylvania, Romania. Its capital city is Brașov.

gem:brasov||Dormition of the Theotokos c.desc: The Brașovechi Church, also known as "The Dormition of the Mother of God" Church (Brașovechi)" is a Romanian Orthodox church located at 47 Bisericii Române Street, Brașov, Romania. Located in the Brașovechi district, it is dedicated to the Dormition of the Theotokos.

gem:sighisoara||Vlad Dracul House.desc: Vlad Dracul House of Sighișoara is located in Tin Street No.1, between the Citadel Square and the Clock Tower. It is the place where Vlad the Impaler, the historical character who inspired Bram Stoker's Dracula, was born, in 1431.

gem:brasov||Hungarian Lutheran church in.desc: Brașov County is a county (județ) of Transylvania, Romania. Its capital city is Brașov.

gem:brasov||Brașov Fortress.desc: Bran Castle is a castle in Bran, 25 kilometres (16 mi) southwest of Brașov. The castle was built by Saxons in 1377 who were given the privilege by Louis I of Hungary.

gem:veliko-tarnovo||Holy Forty Martyrs C.desc: The Holy Forty Martyrs Church is a medieval Eastern Orthodox church constructed in 1230 in the town of Veliko Tarnovo in Bulgaria, the former capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire.

gem:veliko-tarnovo||Church of St Demetri.desc: The Church of Saint Demetrius of Thessaloniki is a medieval Bulgarian Orthodox church in the city of Veliko Tarnovo in central northern Bulgaria, the former capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire.

gem:rila||Rila Monastery.desc: The Monastery of Saint John of Rila, also known as Rila Monastery ("Sveti Ivan Rilski", is the largest and most famous Eastern Orthodox monastery in Bulgaria.

gem:veliko-tarnovo||Patriarchal Cathedra.desc: The Patriarchal Cathedral of the Holy Ascension of the Lord is a former Eastern Orthodox cathedral in the city of Veliko Tarnovo, in north central Bulgaria.

gem:veliko-tarnovo||Transfiguration Mona.desc: The Transfiguration Monastery or the Monastery of the Holy Transfiguration of God is an Eastern Orthodox monastery located in the Dervent gorge of the Yantra River. It lies near the village of Samovodene, seven kilometres north of Veliko Tarnovo, in central northern Bulgaria.

gem:rila||Rila Monastery Ecclesiastical.desc: The Bulgarian Orthodox Church, legally the Patriarchate of Bulgaria, is an autocephalous Eastern Orthodox jurisdiction based in Bulgaria.

gem:veliko-tarnovo||Transfiguration Mona.desc: The Transfiguration Monastery or the Monastery of the Holy Transfiguration of God is an Eastern Orthodox monastery located in the Dervent gorge of the Yantra River. It lies near the village of Samovodene, seven kilometres north of Veliko Tarnovo, in central northern Bulgaria.

gem:rila||The Nativity of the Virgin Chu.desc: The Monastery of Saint John of Rila, also known as Rila Monastery ("Sveti Ivan Rilski", is the largest and most famous Eastern Orthodox monastery in Bulgaria.

gem:veliko-tarnovo||Patriarchal Monaster.desc: The Patriarchal Monastery of the Holy Trinity is a Bulgarian Orthodox monastery in the vicinity of Veliko Tarnovo, north central Bulgaria. Founded in the Middle Ages, it was reconstructed in 1847 and again in the mid-20th century.

gem:berat||Bachelors' Mosque.desc: The Bachelors' Mosque, formerly known as the Sylejman Pasha Mosque, is a mosque located in Berat City, Berat County, Albania.

gem:berat||Berat.desc: Berat is the ninth most populous city of Albania and the seat of Berat County and Berat Municipality. By air, it is 71 kilometres north of Gjirokastër, 70 kilometres west of Korçë, 70 kilometres south of Tirana, and 33 kilometres east of Fier.

gem:sighisoara||Breite Oak Tree Reserve.desc: The Breite Oak Tree Reserve is a 74-hectare (180-acre) nature reserve sitting on a plateau atop Sighișoara, Romania. The largest grassland plateau in Europe, the Breite Reserve has attracted visitors for hundreds of years.

gem:berat||Teqeja e Helvetive.desc: The Halveti Tekke is a tekke, located in Berat, Albania. Completed in 1782 CE, the tekke was designated as a Cultural Monument of Albania and forms part of the Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastër, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.

gem:veliko-tarnovo||House with the Monke.desc: Nikola Fichev, commonly known as Kolyo Ficheto or with his Turkish honorific Usta (Master) Kolyo Ficheto, was a Bulgarian National Revival architect, builder and sculptor born in Dryanovo in 1800.

gem:gjirokaster||Gjirokastër Castle.desc: Gjirokastër Castle is a fortress in Gjirokastër, Albania which also includes a Bektashi tyrbe. Gjirokastër Castle is situated at a height of 336 metres (1,102 ft).

gem:berat||Xhamia Mbret.desc: The King Mosque, also known as the Sultan's Mosque or Sultan Bayezid Mosque, is a mosque located in Berat City, Berat County, Albania.

gem:berat||Porta e Pashait, Berat.desc: The Sanjak of Albania was a second-level administrative unit of the Ottoman Empire between 1415 and 1444. Its mandate included territories of modern central and southern Albania between Krujë to the Kalamas River in northwestern Greece.

gem:gjirokaster||Teqe Mosque.desc: The Teqe Mosque is a former mosque and madrasa, located in Gjirokastër, Albania. The former mosque was designated as a Cultural Monument of Albania in 1973; and forms part of the Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastër, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that was designated in 2005.

gem:gjirokaster||Gjirokastër Mosque.desc: The Bazaar Mosque, also known as the Memi Bey Mosque, is a Sunni mosque located in Gjirokastër, Albania. The mosque was designated as a Cultural Monument of Albania in 1973; and forms part of the Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastër, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.

gem:gjirokaster||Gjirokastër Ethnographi.desc: Gjirokastër Ethnographic Museum is a museum in western Gjirokastër, Albania. The museum, constructed in 1966, is built on the site of communist leader Enver Hoxha's birth home and offers an insight into the traditional lifestyle of the town.

gem:gjirokaster||Zekate House.desc: Zekate House, is a house in Gjirokastër, Albania. The house was built in 1811–1812 by Beqir Zeko, a local Albanian general administrator in Ali Pasha's government.

gem:ksamil||Buthrotum.desc: Butrint was an ancient Greek polis and later Roman city and the seat of an early Christian bishopric in Epirus.

gem:kotor||Natural and Culturo-Historica.desc: The Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor is a World Heritage Site located in Montenegro that was inscribed in 1979. It encompasses the old town of Kotor, the fortifications of Kotor, and the surrounding region of the inner Bay of Kotor.

gem:kotor||Fortifications of Kotor.desc: The fortifications of Kotor are an integrated historical fortification system that protected the medieval town of Kotor containing ramparts, towers, citadels, gates, bastions, forts, cisterns, a castle, and ancillary buildings and structures. They incorporate military architecture of Illyria, the Byzantine Empire, Venice, and Austria.

gem:ksamil||Lake Butrint.desc: Butrint Lagoon is a salt lagoon south of Saranda, Albania, located in direct proximity of the Ionian Sea. It is surrounded by dense forested hills, rocky coast and complemented by saltwater and freshwater marshlands.

gem:ksamil||Ali Pasha Castle.desc: Ali Pasha Castle is a castle in Albania. It is named after Ali Pasha of Tepelenë who resided there until 1820.

gem:kotor||Church of Our Lady of Remedy.desc: The Church of Our Lady of Remedy is a Roman Catholic church located in Kotor, Montenegro, belonging to the Roman Catholic Diocese of Kotor. The church is perched on the slope of St.

gem:kotor||Lovćen.desc: Lovćen is a mountain and national park in southwestern Montenegro. It is the inspiration behind the names Montenegro and Crna Gora, both of which mean 'Black Mountain' and refer to the appearance of Mount Lovćen when covered in dense forests.

gem:gjirokaster||Fico House.desc: Gjirokastër is a city in southern Albania and the seat of Gjirokastër County and Gjirokastër Municipality. It is located in a valley between the Gjerë mountains and the Drino, at 300 metres above sea level.

gem:kotor||Mausoleum of Njegoš.desc: The Mausoleum of Njegoš is a mausoleum interring Petar II Petrović-Njegoš located on the top of Jezerski Vrh Peak on Mount Lovćen.

gem:kotor||Štirovnik.desc: Stirovnik is the highest peak of the Lovćen mountain range in Montenegro with an elevation of 1,749 meters (5,738 ft) above sea level. Its summit is occupied by a telecommunications tower and a military facility that restricts public access.

gem:budva||Jaz Beach.desc: Jaz is a beach in the Budva municipality in Montenegro. It is located 2.5 km west of central Budva.

gem:budva||Stanjevići Monastery.desc: The Stanjevići Monastery is located north of the town of Budva, Montenegro.

gem:budva||Podmaine Monastery.desc: The Podmaine Monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery built in the 15th century by the Crnojević noble family in Podmaine near Budva, Zeta. The monastery has two churches, smaller and older church of Presentation of the Mother of God was built by Crnojević noble family in the 15th century while bigger church was built in 1747.

gem:torshavn||Magnus Cathedral.desc: Magnus Cathedral is a ruined cathedral in the village of Kirkjubøur on the island of Streymoy in the Faroe Islands. The ruins are the largest medieval building in the Faroe Islands.

gem:torshavn||Nordic House in the Faroe.desc: The Nordic House is a cultural institution in the Faroe Islands. Its aim is to support and promote Nordic and Faroese culture, locally and in the Nordic region.

gem:torshavn||Faroe Islands boreal grass.desc: The Faroe Islands boreal grasslands ecoregion covers all of the territory of the Faroe Islands, an archipelago of 18 islands in the North Atlantic, roughly equidistant between Scotland, Norway, and Iceland. The ground cover is mostly grassland and dwarf shrub heath, the remainder is bare ground or sparse vegetation.

gem:torshavn||Skansin.desc: Skansin is a historic fortress in Tórshavn, the capital of the Faroe Islands.

gem:torshavn||Listasavn Føroya.desc: Listasavn Føroya is an art museum in Tórshavn, Faroe Islands, for mostly permanent exhibits of Faroese arts.

gem:bath||Bath Abbey.desc: The Abbey Church of Saint Peter and Saint Paul, commonly known as Bath Abbey, is a parish church of the Church of England and former Benedictine monastery in Bath, Somerset, England.

gem:bath||Pulteney Bridge.desc: Pulteney Bridge is a bridge over the River Avon in Bath, England. It was completed by 1774, and connected the city with land in Bathwick which Sir William Pulteney and his family wished to develop.

gem:bath||Parade Gardens.desc: The Parade Gardens is a grade II listed park in Bath, Somerset, England. The gardens are situated to the south of the Empire Hotel, Bath and 250 yards to the east of Bath Abbey.

gem:bath||Royal National Hospital for Rh.desc: The Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases is a small, specialist NHS hospital on the Royal United Hospital site in Weston, Bath, England.

gem:bath||Cross Bath.desc: The Cross Bath in Bath Street, Bath, Somerset, England, is a historic pool for bathing. The surrounding structure of the pool was built, in the style of Robert Adam by Thomas Baldwin by 1784 and remodelled by John Palmer in 1789.

gem:bath||Grand Pump Room, Bath.desc: The Grand Pump Room is a historic building in the Abbey Churchyard, Bath, Somerset, England. It is adjacent to the Roman Baths and is named because of water that is pumped into the room from the baths' hot springs.

gem:oxford||Carfax Tower.desc: Carfax is the junction of St Aldate's (south), Cornmarket Street (north), Queen Street (west) and the High Street (east) in Oxford, England. It is considered to be the centre of the city.

gem:oxford||Tom Quad.desc: The Great Quadrangle, more popularly known as Tom Quad, is one of the quadrangles of Christ Church, Oxford, England. It is the largest college quad in Oxford, measuring 264 by 261 feet.

gem:oxford||St Michael at the Northgate.desc: St Michael at the North Gate is a church in Cornmarket Street, at the junction with Ship Street, in central Oxford, England. The name derives from the church's location on the site of the north gate of Oxford when it was surrounded by the Oxford city wall.

gem:oxford||St Aldate's Church.desc: St Aldate's is a Church of England parish church in the centre of Oxford, in the Deanery and Diocese of Oxford. The church is on the street named St Aldate's, opposite Christ Church college and next door to Pembroke College.

gem:oxford||The Covered Market.desc: The Covered Market is a historic market with permanent stalls and shops in a large covered structure in central Oxford, England. It was designated a Grade II listed building in 2000.

gem:oxford||Oxford Town Hall.desc: Oxford Town Hall is a public building on the street called St Aldate's in central Oxford, England. It is both the seat of Oxford City Council and a venue for public meetings, entertainment and other events.

gem:oxford||St Ebbe's Church.desc: St Ebbe's is a Church of England parish church in central Oxford, named after the seventh-century abbess Æbbe of Coldingham. The church is within the conservative evangelical tradition and participates in the Anglican Reform movement.

gem:cambridge||Cambridge Corn Exchange.desc: The Corn Exchange is an events and concert venue located on Wheeler Street in Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, England. The structure, which was commissioned as a corn exchange, is a Grade II listed building.

gem:cambridge||St Edward King and Martyr.desc: St Edward King and Martyr is a church located on Peas Hill in central Cambridge, England. It is dedicated to Edward the Martyr, who was King of England from 975 until his murder in 978.

gem:cambridge||Champion of the Thames.desc: The Champion of the Thames is a pub in King Street, Cambridge, England. The pub's name derives from an oarsman who won a sculling race on the Thames before moving to Cambridge in 1860.

gem:cambridge||Cambridge Medical School.desc: The building for the Cambridge Medical School of the University of Cambridge was designed in 1899 by Edward Schroeder Prior. Now the Zoological Laboratory, it is a Grade II listed building.

gem:cambridge||Cambridge Guildhall.desc: Cambridge Guildhall is a civic building in the centre of the historic city of Cambridge, England. It includes two halls, The Large Hall and The Small Hall, and is used for many disparate events such as comedy acts, conferences, craft fairs, live music, talks, and weddings.

gem:cambridge||Sedgwick Museum of Earth.desc: The Sedgwick Museum of Earth Sciences, is the geology museum of the University of Cambridge. It is part of the Department of Earth Sciences and is located on the university's Downing Site in Downing Street, central Cambridge, England.

gem:cambridge||Christ's Pieces.desc: Christ's Pieces or Christ's Piece is a Victorian park in the east of central Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, England, with flower beds, ornamental trees and a memorial garden to Diana, Princess of Wales. The area acts as an important publicly accessible open grassed area for the city centre.

gem:york||Lady Row.desc: Lady Row, also known as Our Lady's Row, is a mediaeval Grade I listed building on Goodramgate in York, England. Historic England describe the structure as "some of the earliest urban vernacular building surviving in England".

gem:york||York Unitarian Chapel.desc: York Unitarian Chapel is a building on St. Saviourgate, York, England.

gem:york||St Crux Parish Hall.desc: St Crux is a parish hall in York, in England, which incorporates the remains of a mediaeval church.

gem:york||The Old White Swan.desc: The Old White Swan is a pub in the city centre of York, in England. The core of the building is timber-framed and was constructed in the early-17th century.

gem:cotswolds||Cotswolds.desc: The Cotswolds is a region of South West and South Central England, along a range of wolds or rolling hills that rise from the meadows of the upper River Thames to an escarpment above the Severn Valley and the Vale of Evesham.

gem:cotswolds||Chedworth Roman Villa.desc: Chedworth Roman Villa is located near Chedworth, Gloucestershire, England and is a scheduled monument. It is one of the largest and most elaborate Roman villas so far discovered in Britain and one with the latest occupation beyond the Roman period.

gem:cotswolds||Crickley Hill and Barrow.desc: Crickley Hill and Barrow Wake is a 56.8-hectare (140-acre) biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1974.

gem:cotswolds||Great Witcombe Roman Vill.desc: Great Witcombe Roman Villa was a villa built during the Roman occupation of Britain. It is located on a hillside at Great Witcombe, near Gloucester in the English county of Gloucestershire.

gem:cotswolds||Edgeworth Manor.desc: Edgeworth Manor is a Grade II* listed country house in Edgeworth, Gloucestershire, England. It was mentioned in the Domesday Book, when it was held by Roger de Lacy.

gem:york||St Sampson's Centre.desc: St Sampson's Church is a former parish church in the city centre of York, England. It lies on Church Street, near St Sampson's Square.

gem:cotswolds||Leckhampton Hill.desc: Leckhampton Hill and Charlton Kings Common is a 63.8-hectare (158-acre) biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954. There are five units of assessment.

gem:york||Newgate Market.desc: Newgate Market can refer to:A market formerly held on Newgate, in London The former name of Shambles Market, in York

gem:cotswolds||Juniper Hill, Edgeworth.desc: Juniper Hill, Edgeworth is an 11.25-hectare (27.8-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1974. The site is listed in the 'Cotswold District' Local Plan 2001-2011 as a Key Wildlife Site (KWS).

gem:lake-district||Allan Bank.desc: Allan Bank is a grade II listed two-storey villa standing on high ground slightly to the west of Grasmere village in the heart of the Lake District.

gem:lake-district||Dove Cottage.desc: Dove Cottage is a house on the edge of Grasmere in the Lake District of England. It is best known as the home of the poet William Wordsworth and his sister Dorothy Wordsworth from December 1799 to May 1808, where they spent over eight years of "plain living, but high thinking".

gem:lake-district||Lake District Nationa.desc: The Lake District, also known as the Lakes or Lakeland, is a mountainous region and national park in Cumbria, North West England. It is famous for its landscape, including its lakes, coast, and mountains, and for its literary associations with Beatrix Potter, John Ruskin, Arthur Ransome, and the Lake Poets.

gem:cotswolds||Knap House Quarry, Birdli.desc: Knap House Quarry, Birdlip is a 1.80-hectare (4.4-acre) geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1974. The site is listed in the 'Cotswold District' Local Plan 2001-2011 as a Key Wildlife Site (KWS) and a Regionally Important Geological Site (RIGS).

gem:lake-district||Elter Water.desc: Elter Water is a small lake in the Lake District in North West England, half a mile southeast of the village of the same name. It has a length of 0.62 miles (1.00 km), maximum width of approximately 0.24 miles (0.39 km), a maximum depth of 7 metres (7.7 yd), and an area of 0.16 square kilometres (0.062 sq mi).

gem:lake-district||Langdale Boulders.desc: The Langdale Boulders are a pair of natural boulders at the southeastern end of the Langdale Valley, just northwest of Chapel Stile. They are also known locally as the "Copt Howe" boulders.

gem:lake-district||Bowfell.desc: Bowfell is a pyramid-shaped mountain lying at the heart of the English Lake District, in the Southern Fells area. It is the eighth-highest mountain in the Lake District and one of the most popular of the Lake District fells for walkers.

gem:lake-district||Lingmoor Fell.desc: Lingmoor Fell is a fell in the English Lake District, situated eight kilometres west of Ambleside. The fell reaches a height of 469 m (1,540 ft) and divides the valleys of Great Langdale and Little Langdale.

gem:cotswolds||Rough Bank, Miserden.desc: Rough Bank, Miserden is a 9.2-hectare (23-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1986. It was purchased by the wildlife charity Butterfly Conservation in 2012.

gem:isle-of-skye||Fairy Pools.desc: The Fairy Pools (Scottish Gaelic: Glumagan nan Sithichean) are a series of natural pools and waterfalls in Glen Brittle on the Isle of Skye, Scotland. They are in Coire na Creiche, on the Allt Coir' a' Mhadaidh, at the foot of the Cuillin mountains.

gem:isle-of-skye||Battle of Coire Na Cre.desc: The Battle of Coire na Creiche was a Scottish clan battle fought on the Isle of Skye in 1601. It was the culmination of a year of feuding between Clan MacLeod of Dunvegan and the Clan MacDonald of Sleat, that ended with a MacDonald victory in Coire na Creiche on the northern slopes of the Cuillin hills.

gem:isle-of-skye||Sgùrr Alasdair.desc: Sgùrr Alasdair is the highest peak of the Black Cuillin, and the highest peak on the Isle of Skye and in the Inner Hebrides, and indeed in all the Scottish islands, at 992 m (3,255 ft). Like the rest of the range it is composed of gabbro, a rock with excellent grip for mountaineering.

gem:isle-of-skye||Sgùrr Dearg.desc: Sgùrr Dearg is a mountain in the Cuillin on the Isle of Skye, Scotland. It is topped by the Inaccessible Pinnacle, a fin of rock measuring 50 metres (160 ft) along its longest edge.

gem:isle-of-skye||Sgùrr nan Gillean.desc: Sgùrr nan Gillean is a peak in the northern part of the Cuillin mountains on the Isle of Skye in Scotland. With a height of 966 metres, it is one of eleven Munros in the Cuillins.

gem:st-ives||St Erth.desc: St Erth is a civil parish and village in Cornwall, England, United Kingdom.

gem:st-ives||The Bucket of Blood.desc: The Bucket of Blood is a public house in Phillack, Hayle, Cornwall, owned by St Austell Brewery and currently tenanted by Nick and Tanya Swanson. It is thought to be named after an incident where the landlord brought up a bucket of blood from the building's well.

gem:st-ives||The Sloop Inn.desc: The Sloop Inn is an inn in St Ives, Cornwall, England, located on the wharf. It is one of the oldest inns in Cornwall, the public house is dated to "circa 1312" although the present building was built in the 17th or 18th century.

gem:st-ives||Barbara Hepworth Museum and.desc: The Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden in St Ives, Cornwall preserves the 20th-century sculptor Barbara Hepworth's studio and garden much as they were when she lived and worked there. She purchased the site in 1949 and lived and worked there for 26 years until her death in a fire on the premises in 1975.

gem:st-ives||Zennor Quoit.desc: Zennor Quoit is a ruined megalithic burial chamber or dolmen, located on a moor about a mile (1.6 km) east of the village of Zennor, Cornwall, England, UK. It dates to 2500–1500 BC.

gem:galway-cliffs||Galway Cathedral.desc: The Cathedral of Our Lady Assumed into Heaven and St Nicholas, commonly known as Galway Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Galway, Ireland.

gem:galway-cliffs||Spanish Arch.desc: The Spanish Arch and the Caoċ Arch in Galway city, Ireland, are two remaining arches on the Ceann an Bhalla.

gem:galway-cliffs||Menlo Castle.desc: Menlo Castle or Menlough Castle, also called Blake's Castle, is a 16th-century castle situated on the bank of the River Corrib near Menlo village in County Galway, Ireland.

gem:cotswolds||Cotswold Commons and Beec.desc: Cotswold Commons and Beechwoods is a 665.5-hectare (1,644-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954.

gem:st-ives||St Ives Parish Church.desc: St Ives is a seaside town, civil parish and port in Cornwall, England, United Kingdom. The town lies north of Penzance and west of Camborne on the coast of the Celtic Sea.

gem:galway-cliffs||Lynch's Castle.desc: Lynch's Castle is a fortified townhouse in Galway City, Ireland. It was built by the Lynch family, which was one of the Tribes of Galway.

gem:galway-cliffs||Galway City Museum.desc: Galway City Museum is a museum in Galway City, County Galway, Ireland. It was founded on 29 July 2006, and is located beside the Spanish Arch.

gem:st-ives||Trencrom Hill Fort.desc: Trencrom Hill is a prominent hill fort, owned by the National Trust, near Lelant, Cornwall. It is crowned by an univallate Neolithic tor enclosure and was re-used as a hillfort in the Iron Age.

gem:dingle||Gallarus Oratory.desc: The Gallarus Oratory is an oratory on the Dingle Peninsula, County Kerry, Ireland. gem:dingle||Conor Pass.desc: The Conor Pass or Connor Pass is one of the highest mountain passes in Ireland served by an asphalted road. It is on the R560 road on the Dingle Peninsula in County Kerry.

gem:connemara||Connemara National Park.desc: Connemara National Park is one of eight national parks in Ireland, managed by the National Parks and Wildlife Service. It is located in the northwest of Connemara in County Galway, on the west coast.

gem:connemara||Benbaun.desc: Benbaun is a mountain in County Galway, Ireland. With a height of 729 metres (2,392 ft), it is the 72nd highest peak in Ireland on the Arderin scale, and the 88th highest peak on the Vandeleur-Lynam scale.

gem:connemara||Kylemore Abbey.desc: Kylemore Abbey is a Benedictine Monastery founded in 1920 on the grounds of Kylemore Castle, in Connemara, County Galway, Ireland. The Abbey was founded for Benedictine nuns who fled Belgium in World War 1.

gem:zakopane||Zakopane.desc: Zakopane is a town in the south of Poland, in the southern part of the Podhale region at the foot of the Tatra Mountains. From 1975 to 1998, it was part of Nowy Sącz Voivodeship; since 1999, it has been part of Lesser Poland Voivodeship.

gem:zakopane||Villa Atma.desc: The Villa Atma in Zakopane, Poland, is a historic chalet housing the Karol Szymanowski Museum, department of the National Museum in Kraków.

gem:zakopane||Museum of Zakopane Style a.desc: The Museum of Zakopane Style at Villa Koliba is a division of the Tatra Museum in Zakopane, and a museum of Zakopane style.

gem:zakopane||Gubałówka.desc: Gubałówka is a mountain in the Gubałówka Range, above the Polish town of Zakopane. The mountain is a popular tourist attraction, offering commanding views of the Tatras and Zakopane.

gem:high-tatras||Rysy.desc: Rysy is a mountain in the crest of the High Tatras, eastern part of the Tatra Mountains, located on the border between Poland and Slovakia. gem:high-tatras||Veľký Mengusovský štít.desc: Mięguszowiecki Szczyt Wielki or the Mięguszowiecki Grand Peak is a mountain in the Tatra Mountains, located on the border between Poland and Slovakia.

gem:high-tatras||Cubryna.desc: Cubryna is a mountain in the High Tatras mountain range, situated on the main ridge of the Tatras between Mięguszowiecki Szczyt Wielki and Zadni Mnich, on the border between Poland and Slovakia. At 2376 meters, it's one of the highest peaks in Poland.

gem:high-tatras||Niżnie Rysy.desc: Niżnie Rysy is a mountain made up of four granite peaks, the highest of which has an elevation of 2430 meters, making it overall the third highest mountain in Poland. gem:auschwitz||German Nazi Concentration.desc: Monowitz was a Nazi concentration camp and labor camp (Arbeitslager) run by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland from 1942 to 1945, during World War II and the Holocaust.

gem:high-tatras||Mięguszowiecki Szczyt C.desc: Mięguszowiecki Szczyt Czarny is a mountain situated on the main ridge of the Tatra Mountains in the High Tatras mountain range on the border between Poland and Slovakia and is the easternmost of the three Mięguszowiecki Summits. Its peak has an elevation of 2404 meters, making it the fourth highest mountain in Poland.

gem:masuria||Mazurski Park Krajobrazowy.desc: Masurian Landscape Park is a designated Polish Landscape Park protected area within Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship, in northern Poland. It is one of the largest landscape parks in Poland.

gem:vaduz||Liechtensteinische Landesbank.desc: Liechtensteinische Landesbank AG, trading as LLB, is a financial institution located in Liechtenstein, based in the capital city Vaduz. gem:bath||Guildhall, Bath.desc: Guildhall is an 18th-century municipal building in central Bath, Somerset, England. It is a Grade I listed building.

gem:high-tatras||Mięguszowiecki Szczyt P.desc: Mięguszowiecki Szczyt Pośredni is a mountain situated on the main ridge of the Tatra Mountains in the High Tatras mountain range on the border between Poland and Slovakia. It's the lowest of the three Mięguszowiecki Summits and it is located in the middle of the group.

gem:vaduz||Liechtenstein National Museum.desc: The Liechtenstein National Museum is a museum in Vaduz, the capital city of Liechtenstein.

gem:vaduz||Vaduz Castle.desc: Vaduz Castle is the palace and official residence of the Prince of Liechtenstein. The castle gave its name to the town of Vaduz, the capital of Liechtenstein, which it overlooks from an adjacent hilltop.

gem:andorra-la-vella||Casa de la Vall.desc: Casa de la Vall is a historical house in Andorra la Vella, Andorra. It was the seat of the General Council of Andorra until 2011.

gem:andorra-la-vella||Casa Felipó.desc: Casa Felipó is a historical building in Andorra la Vella, Andorra. Built in 1948, it is located along the Avinguda de Meritxell, just to east of the Andorra National Library and the Església de Sant Esteve.

gem:andorra-la-vella||església de Santa.desc: The Church of Santa Coloma d'Andorra is a church in Santa Coloma, Andorra la Vella Parish, Andorra, and is Andorra's oldest church. It is a heritage property registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra.

gem:andorra-la-vella||Casa Palmitjavila.desc: Casa Palmitjavila is a town house located at Avinguda Carlemany, 79 Escaldes, Escaldes–Engordany Parish, Andorra. It is a heritage property registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra.

gem:andorra-la-vella||Antiga Vegueria Fr.desc: Antiga Vegueria Francesa is a historical house located at Avinguda Meritxell, 13 in Andorra la Vella, Andorra. It is a heritage property registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra.

gem:vaduz||Kathedrale St. Florin.desc: Vaduz Cathedral, or Cathedral of St. Florin, is a neo-Gothic church in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, and the centre of the Archdiocese of Vaduz.

gem:san-marino||Basilica di San Marino.desc: The Basilica of Saint Marinus is a Catholic church located in the Republic of San Marino. While the country has a distinct domination of historic religious buildings of Christian faith, the basilica is the main church of the City of San Marino.

gem:san-marino||The Three Towers of San.desc: The Three Towers of San Marino are a group of towers located in San Marino. Located on the three peaks of Monte Titano in the capital, also called San Marino, they are depicted on both the national flag and coat of arms.

gem:san-marino||Monte Titano.desc: Monte Titano or Monte Brugola is a mountain of the Apennines and the highest point in the country of San Marino. gem:san-marino||Statua della Libertà.desc: Statua della Libertà is a statue in Piazza della Libertà, City of San Marino, the capital city of the Republic of San Marino.

gem:monaco-mc||Monaco Cemetery.desc: The Monaco Cemetery is a cemetery in La Colle, Principality of Monaco.

gem:monaco-mc||Prince's Palace of Monaco.desc: The Prince's Palace of Monaco is the official residence of the Sovereign Prince of Monaco. Built in 1191 as a Genoese fortress, during its long and often dramatic history it has been bombarded and besieged by many foreign powers.

gem:san-marino||Guaita.desc: The Guaita, also known as the Rocca is one of three towered peaks overlooking the city of San Marino, the capital of San Marino. The other two are Cesta and Montale.

gem:monaco-mc||Rock of Monaco.desc: The Rock of Monaco is a 62-metre (203 ft) tall monolith on the Mediterranean coast of the Principality of Monaco. It overlooks the Mediterranean Sea and the Port Hercules.

gem:leuven||Leuven Town Hall.desc: The Town Hall of Leuven, Flemish Brabant, Belgium, is a landmark building on that city's Grote Markt, across from the monumental St. Peter's Church.

gem:leuven||Heilige-Geestcollege.desc: Holy Spirit College was one of the colleges of Leuven University, now listed as built heritage of Flanders, Belgium.

gem:dinant||Castle of Freÿr.desc: The Castle of Freÿr with its gardens in the style of Le Nôtre is located in Wallonia on the left bank of the Meuse, between Waulsort and Dinant. They form one of the most magnificent natural sites in Belgium.

gem:kinderdijk||Mill Network at Kinderdi.desc: The Kinderdijk windmills are a group of 19 monumental windmills in the Alblasserwaard polder, in the province of South Holland, Netherlands. gem:kinderdijk||Krimpen aan de Lek.desc: Krimpen aan de Lek is a village on the Lek River in the municipality of Krimpenerwaard, province of South Holland, the Netherlands. It had 6,607 inhabitants in 2008.

gem:killarney||Muckross Abbey.desc: Muckross Abbey is a ruined Franciscan friary located in the Killarney National Park, County Kerry, Ireland. Previously known as the "Friary of Irrelagh", the abbey was founded in 1448 for the Observantine Franciscans by Donal McCarthy Mor.

gem:leiden||De Waag.desc: Pieter Jansz Post was a Dutch Golden Age architect, painter and printmaker.

gem:kilkenny||Kilkenny Castle.desc: Kilkenny Castle is a castle in Kilkenny, Ireland, built in 1260 to control a fording-point of the River Nore and the junction of several routeways.

gem:doolin||Cliffs of Moher.desc: The Cliffs of Moher are sea cliffs located at the southwestern edge of the Burren region in County Clare, Ireland. They run for about 14 kilometres.

gem:kilkenny||Saint Canice's Cathedral.desc: St Canice's Cathedral, also known as Kilkenny Cathedral, is a Church of Ireland cathedral in Kilkenny city, Ireland. It is in the ecclesiastical province of Dublin.

gem:doolin||O'Brien's Tower.desc: O'Brien's Tower marks the highest point of the Cliffs of Moher in County Clare, Ireland. It is located a short distance from the villages Doolin and Liscannor.

gem:doolin||Doonagore Castle.desc: Doonagore Castle is a round 16th-century tower house with a small walled enclosure located about 1 km south of the coastal village of Doolin in County Clare, Ireland. gem:aran-islands||Dun Aengus.desc: Dún Aonghasa is the best-known of several prehistoric hill forts on the Aran Islands of County Galway, Ireland. It lies on Inis Mór, at the edge of a 100-metre-high (330 ft) cliff.

gem:aran-islands||Dun Arann Lighthouse.desc: Inishmore is the largest of the Aran Islands in Galway Bay, off the west coast of Ireland. With an area of 31 km2 (12 sq mi) and a population of 820, it is the second-largest island off the Irish coast and most populous of the Aran Islands.

gem:st-wolfgang||Sankt Gilgen.desc: Sankt Gilgen is a village by Lake Wolfgang in the Austrian state of Salzburg, in the Salzkammergut region.

gem:montreux||Montreux.desc: Montreux is a Swiss municipality and town on the shoreline of Lake Geneva at the foot of the Alps. gem:montreux||Chillon Castle.desc: Chillon Castle is a medieval island castle located on Lake Geneva, south of Veytaux in the Swiss canton of Vaud. gem:lausanne||Palais de Rumine.desc: The Palais de Rumine is a late 19th-century building in Florentine Renaissance style in Lausanne, Switzerland.

gem:lausanne||mudac.desc: The Museum of Contemporary Design and Applied Arts is a museum in Lausanne, Switzerland.

gem:lugano||Museo d'arte della Svizzera.desc: The Swiss–Italian Art Museum, commonly known as MASI Lugano, MASILugano or MASI, is an art museum predominantly featuring 20th-century and contemporary art in Lugano, Switzerland. gem:lugano||Lugano Arte e Cultura.desc: Lugano Arte e Cultura (LAC) is a polyfunctional cultural centre dedicated to music, visual and performance arts in Lugano, Switzerland. It houses the Museo d'arte della Svizzera italiana and hosts events such as "LuganoInScena" and "LuganoMusica".

gem:appenzell||Appenzell.desc: Appenzell was a canton in the northeast of Switzerland, and entirely surrounded by the canton of St. Gallen, in existence from 1403 to 1597.

gem:coimbra||Coimbra.desc: Coimbra, officially the City of Coimbra, is a city and a municipality in Portugal. The population of the municipality at the 2021 census was 140,796, in an area of 319.40 square kilometres (123.3 sq mi).

gem:appenzell||Schloss Appenzell.desc: Appenzell Castle is a castle in the Appenzell District of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden in Switzerland. It is one of a few 16th century stone buildings in Appenzell.

gem:coimbra||Mosteiro de Santa Cruz.desc: The Monastery of the Holy Cross, also known as the Church of the Holy Cross, is a National Monument in Coimbra, Portugal. Because the first two kings of Portugal are buried in the church, it was granted the status of National Pantheon.

gem:coimbra||Monastery of Santa Cruz.desc: The Monastery of the Holy Cross, also known as the Church of the Holy Cross, is a National Monument in Coimbra, Portugal. Because the first two kings of Portugal are buried in the church, it was granted the status of National Pantheon.

gem:lagos-pt||Ponta da Piedade.desc: Ponta da Piedade is a headland with a group of rock formations along the coastline of the town of Lagos, in the Portuguese region of the Algarve. gem:coimbra||New Cathedral of Coimbra.desc: The New Cathedral of Coimbra, also referred to as Cathedral of the Holy Name of Jesus, is currently bishopric co-seat, along with the Old Cathedral of Coimbra, of the city of Coimbra, in Portugal. gem:lagos-pt||Estação Arqueológica de Mo.desc: Monte Molião is an archaeological site located in the Municipality of Lagos, in Portugal . The site is located on Monte Molião, an elevation north-west of Lagos city center, on the east bank of the Ribeira de Bensafrim, in the parish of São Sebastião.

gem:tavira||Castelo de Tavira.desc: The Castle of Tavira is a medieval castle located in the parish of Santiago, Tavira municipality, Faro district of Portugal.

gem:tavira||Igreja da Misericórdia de Ta.desc: Igreja da Misericórdia de Tavira is a church in the Algarve region of Portugal. It is classified as a National Monument.

gem:tavira||Forte do Rato.desc: Fort Santo António of Tavira, also known as Rato Fort or Lebres Island Fort, is located east of the Quatro Águas site, at the mouth of the Gilão River, next to the bar of the city of Tavira, in the District of Faro, in Portugal.

gem:aveiro||Cathedral of Aveiro.desc: The Cathedral of Aveiro, also known as the Church of St. Dominic, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Aveiro, Portugal.

gem:aveiro||Church of São João Evangelis.desc: A Church of São João Evangelista, or Carmelite Church of Aveiro, is an 18th-century church in the Praça Marquês de Pombal, in the civil parish of Glória e Vera Cruz, in the Portuguese municipality of Aveiro. It was declared a national monument in 1910.

gem:tavira||Forte de São João da Barra.desc: The Fort São João da Barra also known as Fort São João Baptista or Fort Conceição, is located to the east of the town of Cabanas de Tavira, on a small hill below the Ria Formosa in the municipality of Tavira, in Algarve, southern Portugal.

gem:aveiro||Aveiro.desc: Aveiro is a city and a municipality in Portugal. In 2021, the population was 80,880, in an area of 197.58 square kilometres (76.29 mi2): it is the second most populous city in the Centro Region of Portugal.

gem:monsaraz||Monsaraz.desc: Monsaraz is a civil parish (freguesia) of the municipality of Reguengos de Monsaraz, on the right margin of the Guadiana River in the Portuguese Alentejo region, near its border with Spain. The population in 2011 was 782, in an area of 88.29 km2.

gem:monsaraz||Castle of Mourão.desc: The Castle of Mourão is a well-preserved castle in the town of Mourão, Portugal. It is classified by IGESPAR as a Site of Public Interest.

gem:tomar||Convent of Christ.desc: The Convent of Christ of Tomar, also called Convent of Christ or Monastery of Christ, is a former Catholic convent in Tomar, Portugal.

gem:tomar||Castelo de Tomar.desc: Tomar Castle is a national monument in the Santarém District of Portugal. Built on a hill above the town of Tomar and the river Nabão on land donated by King Afonso Henriques it was the Portuguese headquarters of the Knights Templar and the residence of their Grand Prior or Preceptor.

gem:monsaraz||Menir da Abelhoa.desc: The Menhir of Bulhoa, also known as the Menhir of Abelhoa, is a granite megalithic standing stone, located near the parish of Monsaraz, in the municipality of the Reguengos de Monsaraz, in the Évora district of the Alentejo region of Portugal. It was classified as a National Monument by the Government of Portugal in 1971.

gem:tomar||Sinagoga de Tomar.desc: The Synagogue of Tomar is a former Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 73 Rua Dr. Joaquim Jaquinto, in the historic center of the city of Tomar, in the Santarém District of Portugal.

gem:tomar||Igreja de Santa Maria dos Oli.desc: The Church of Santa Maria do Olival is a Roman Catholic church in the city of Tomar, in Portugal. The Church has been characterized as National Monument since 1910.

gem:pecs||Yakovalı Hasan Paşa Mosque.desc: The Yakovalı Hasan Paşa Mosque is an early 17th-century mosque in Pécs, southern Hungary. It was constructed when the region was part of the Turkish Ottoman Empire, together with the main mosque of Pécs, the Mosque of Pasha Qasim.

gem:pecs||Klimo Library.desc: The Klimo Library, Klimo Collection or Episcopal Library established in 1774 is the first public library of Hungary. It was established in Pécs by György Klimó, Bishop of Pécs and it is still operating.

gem:tomar||Aqueduto do Convento de Crist.desc: The Convent of Christ Aqueduct, also known as the Pegões Aqueduct, was built to supply water to the Convent of Christ in Tomar from four different springs. It is approximately 6 km long.

gem:tomar||Aqueduto dos Pegões.desc: The Convent of Christ Aqueduct, also known as the Pegões Aqueduct, was built to supply water to the Convent of Christ in Tomar from four different springs. It is approximately 6 km long.

gem:szeged||Szeged Synagogue.desc: The Szeged Synagogue, also called the Great Synagogue and the New Synagogue, is a Neolog Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at Josika ut. 10, in Szeged, in the county of Csongrád-Csanád, Hungary.

gem:szeged||Votive Church of Szeged.desc: The Votive Church and Cathedral of Our Lady of Hungary is a twin-spired church in Szeged. It lies on Dóm square beside the Dömötör tower.

gem:szeged||Belvárosi híd (Szeged).desc: The Belvárosi Bridge in Szeged, Hungary, is the main bridge of the city, connecting Újszeged, on the left bank of the river Tisza, to the other quarters. It was the only crossing on the river in the County until the finishing of the Bertalan Bridge in 1979.

gem:pecs||Early Christian Necropolis of.desc: The Early Christian Necropolis of Pécs is a Roman cemetery and archeological site in Pécs, Hungary. Dating from the 4th century AD, the necropolis contains many decorated tombs, mausoleums, and burial chapels from the Early Christian period.

gem:szeged||Dömötör Tower.desc: The Dömötör tower is the oldest building in Szeged, Hungary. The foundation was most probably laid during the 11th century, while the lower part was built from the 12th century, and the upper part from the 13th century.

gem:szeged||Móra Ferenc Múzeum.desc: The Móra Ferenc Museum is a museum in Szeged, Hungary. The museum stands at the intersection of the bank of the river Tisza and the city's Downtown Bridge.

gem:pecs||Gymnasium of Cistercian Order.desc: This list includes past and present buildings, facilities and institutions associated with the Society of Jesus. In each country, sites are listed in chronological order of start of the Jesuit association.
